Routes are registered with .get() / .post() / .put() and\n// matched in registration order. The first route with a matching method and URL\n// wins, and its captured path segments are passed to the handler as positional\n// arguments.\n//\n// Routing preserves the original behavior of the cumulative evaluator suite:\n//   - ----------\n\nfunction activeCombatant(session) {\n  const c = session.order[session.turn_index];\n  return { name: c.name, score: c.score };\n}\n\nfunction publicOrder(order) {\n  return order.map(c Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n server.js   ──▶  lib/router.js  ──▶  lib/handlers.js\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────┐\n              ▼                                   ▼\n       lib/db.js                            lib/domain.js\n    (SQLite + schema)                      (pure logic)\n              │\n              ▼\n       lib/http.js\n  (responses + body reading)\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses.
